evidence_timeline.summary: We summarize the observations from the most recent ZTF experiment (AstroNote 2024-266, the Nightly-cadence Three-band Extragalactic Survey), conducted from 2024-09-22 02:38 UT to 2024-09-24 12:43 UT. A total of 78 extragalactic transients were identified. Of the 41 transients that met our selection criteria for spectroscopic follow-up, 38 were classified, while two were observed but remain unclassified, resulting in a classification completeness of 95% and a spectroscopic completeness of 97.6%.

publication_revisions.abstract: We summarize the observations from the most recent ZTF experiment (AstroNote 2024-266, the Nightly-cadence Three-band Extragalactic Survey), conducted from 2024-09-22 02:38 UT to 2024-09-24 12:43 UT. A total of 78 extragalactic transients were identified. Of the 41 transients that met our selection criteria for spectroscopic follow-up, 38 were classified, while two were observed but remain unclassified, resulting in a classification completeness of 95% and a spectroscopic completeness of 97.6%.
publication_revisions.authors_text: Qin, Y.; Fremling, C.; Nordin, J.; Gkini, A.; Sollerman, J.; Schulze, S.; Rehemtulla, N.; Miller, A.; Perley, D.

parameters.detrending: magnitudes minus the chosen multiband fit when one exists (a transient's own rise and fall is not a period)

runs.claimBoundary: SALT3 light-curve parameters assuming a normal type Ia supernova; not a classification or a distance.

parameters.phaseWindowDays: detections from 20 days before to 50 days after the brightest detection, times (1+z) (z = 0.1 when fitted)
parameters.selectionRule: TNS classification containing 'Ia', or a broker reading of SN Ia

runs.claimBoundary: Screens that point at candidates for a closer look (kilonova-like timescales, nuclear position); they are not classifications.
